user: What is an OOV word?
assistant: An out-of-vocabulary (OOV) word is a term used in the context of speech recognition services. It refers to a word that is not already part of the service's base vocabulary. When you add a grammar file to a custom language model, the service identifies OOV words and adds them to the custom model's words resource. The purpose of the words resource is to define words that are not already present in the service's vocabulary. Definitions in the words resource tell the service how to transcribe the OOV words.
[The End of Previous Conversation]

[The Start of Current Turn Question]
What is a customization interface?
[The End of Current Turn Question]

[The Start of Reference Answer]
The IBM Watson® Speech-to-Text service provides a customization interface that allows you to enhance its speech recognition capabilities. By customizing a base model for your specific domain and audio, you can improve the accuracy of speech recognition requests. The Text-to-Speech service also includes a customization feature that creates a dictionary of words and their pronunciations for a particular language. This dictionary is known as a custom model. Each entry in a custom model consists of a word and its corresponding pronunciation. The pronunciation guides the service on how to articulate the word when it appears in the input text.
[The End of Reference Answer]

[The Start of Assistant's Answer]
A customization interface is a set of methods for creating, managing, and using custom models to adapt a service’s behavior.

For IBM Watson Speech to Text, it lets you customize a base model for your domain and audio to improve speech recognition accuracy. It supports both custom language models and custom acoustic models; you use a model in a recognition request by specifying its customization ID. [S1][S2]

For speech synthesis, the interface lets you create and manage custom models containing word/translation pairs that tell the service how to pronounce words. [S4][S5]
[The End of Assistant's Answer]

[The Start of Document]
Understanding customization 

The IBM Watson® Speech to Text service offers a customization interface that you can use to augment its speech recognition capabilities. You can use customization to improve the accuracy of speech recognition requests by customizing a base model for your domain and audio.

The customization interface supports both custom language models and custom acoustic models. The interfaces for both types of custom model are similar and straightforward to use. Using either type of custom model with a recognition request is also straightforward: You specify the customization ID of the model with the request.

Speech recognition works the same with or without a custom model.

The customization interface provides methods to create and manage your custom models, which the service stores permanently. After you create a custom model, you can use it during synthesis with any version of the /v1/synthesize method. When the service synthesizes input text, it determines the pronunciation of words that appear in the custom model by applying their translations either directly or indirectly. Because you create a custom model for a specific language, a custom model can be used with any voice that is available in that language.
